theory.title: Exercise 2.4.4: ENUMERATE Iteration
theory.content:
🔢 Indexed Iteration

MENTOR-9: "You've iterated through values. You've used numeric ranges. Now combine them: ENUMERATE gives you BOTH index and value!"

"Perfect for numbered lists, progress tracking, and reports."

📘 ENUMERATE Syntax

Basic Form:

# Default (index starts at 0)
FOR    ${index}    ${value}    IN ENUMERATE    @{list}
    Log    Item ${index}: ${value}
END

# Custom start (1-based numbering)
FOR    ${index}    ${value}    IN ENUMERATE    @{list}    start=1
    Log    Item ${index}: ${value}
END
  • ${index} - First variable (position in list)
  • ${value} - Second variable (item from list)
  • IN ENUMERATE - Special iteration mode
  • start=N - Optional starting index (default 0)

💡 ENUMERATE Examples

# 0-based (default)
@{colors}=    Create List    red    green    blue
FOR    ${i}    ${color}    IN ENUMERATE    @{colors}
    Log    Color ${i}: ${color}
END
# Output: Color 0: red, Color 1: green, Color 2: blue

# 1-based (start=1)
@{tasks}=    Create List    Boot    Check    Report
FOR    ${step}    ${task}    IN ENUMERATE    @{tasks}    start=1
    Log    Step ${step}: ${task}
END
# Output: Step 1: Boot, Step 2: Check, Step 3: Report

# Custom start
FOR    ${i}    ${val}    IN ENUMERATE    @{items}    start=100
    Log    Item ${i}: ${val}
END
# Output: Item 100: ..., Item 101: ..., etc.

⚙️ Key Rules

  • 🔹 Two variables required: ${index} and ${value}
  • 🔹 Order matters: Index FIRST, value SECOND
  • 🔹 Default start=0: Like Python/C indexing
  • 🔹 start=1 common: For user-friendly numbering

🎯 Your Task

Create an enumerated list of systems starting at 1: "System 1: power", "System 2: sensors", etc.
